provenance.citation: Sussman, Gerald Jay. "A Computational Model of Skill Acquisition." MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Technical Report AI TR-297, August 1973. Thesis Supervisor: Seymour A. Papert.
provenance.locus: Chapter II "The Scenario", Sections 1–5 (pp. 17–37). The five Scenario sections are the curriculum: Section 1 (CLEARTOP prerequisite), Section 2 (bottom-up ON-chain ordering), Section 3 (space allocation), Section 4 (unstated page 84), Section 5 (unstated page 94). Problems 1.1, 1.3 are solved without error (achieved); Problem 1.2 triggers a CLEARTOP bug/patch (achieved after patch); Problem 2.1 triggers the bottom-up ordering bug/patch (achieved after patch); Problems 3.x introduce space-allocation bugs still being learned (not all achieved at any given curriculum step).
provenance.notes: The existing fixture in breed-inputs-real.ts uses opaque labels (sub-goal-0 through sub-goal-4) and only encodes achieved state via facts. This improved version maps each goal to a named HACKER Scenario section with paper-grounded descriptions, adds partial-belief facts reflecting how much of each patch HACKER has internalised, and adds a rules array encoding the four main caveats HACKER acquires (CLEARTOP, bottom-up ordering, compact-then-place, flush-before-compact). The state array reflects the canonical 3-block scene from Section 2. Goals g0 and g1 are marked achieved (facts). Goals g2–g4 remain unachieved. The breed should recommend g2 as the next prerequisite to tackle.

expected.rationale: Goals g0 (CLEARTOP patch) and g1 (bottom-up ON-chain ordering patch) are achieved. The next unachieved goal in curriculum order is g2: mastering space allocation via compacting (Section 3, Problems 3.1–3.5). The breed should recommend tackling g2 next because its belief score (0.5) is partially known and it is the lowest-index unachieved goal. Goals g3 and g4 depend on g2 being mastered first.

paper_problem_mapping.g0: Problems 1.1–1.4: HACKER learns CLEARTOP — when placing block X on Y, first remove anything on top of X (patch applied in Problem 1.2 after primitive error, generalised and confirmed working in 1.3 and 1.4)
paper_problem_mapping.g1: Problems 2.1–2.2: HACKER learns ON-chains must be built bottom-up — conjunctive goal (ON A B) AND (ON B C) must achieve (ON B C) before (ON A B), not sequentially top-down; bug detected in 2.1, patch interchanges steps, confirmed in 2.2
paper_problem_mapping.g2: Problems 3.1–3.5: HACKER learns space allocation — when destination surface has insufficient room, try compacting (push existing blocks to one side) before placing; compacting strategy learned incrementally
paper_problem_mapping.g3: Problems 3.4–3.6: HACKER learns flushing must precede compacting when PROTECT constraints are active — non-optimal compacting-first order exposed as bug when PROTECT annotation is present
paper_problem_mapping.g4: Sections 4–5: Higher-order protection and anomalous situation handling — not yet reached in the curriculum at the snapshot point encoded in this fixture
